title: ESO Guideline 2025 Update: Blood Pressure Management in Acute Ischaemic Stroke and Intracerebral Haemorrhage
shortTitle: ESO BP in Acute Stroke 2025 update

recommendations.text: Routine prehospital blood pressure reduction is not recommended in suspected acute stroke.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 1; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Avoid transdermal glyceryl trinitrate because it may harm patients with ICH. Intravenous urapidil or labetalol may be preferred if blood pressure treatment is used. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 1; consensus 1

recommendations.text: For hospitalised AIS with blood pressure <220/110 mmHg and no IVT or thrombectomy, avoid routine blood pressure reduction during at least the first 24 hours after onset unless a specific comorbidity requires it.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 2; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: For AIS without IVT or thrombectomy and blood pressure >220/120 mmHg, cautious reduction by <15% in systolic pressure over 24 hours is reasonable and likely safe. No particular agent is supported. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 2; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 3: IV thrombolysis blood pressure limits
recommendations.text: For AIS receiving IVT, with or without thrombectomy, maintain blood pressure <185/110 mmHg before the bolus and <180/105 mmHg afterward for 24 hours. Evidence does not identify a preferred agent.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 3; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: After IVT, with or without thrombectomy, avoid targeting systolic pressure 130–140 mmHg rather than <180 mmHg during the first 72 hours after stroke onset.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 3; recommendation 2

recommendations.text: During thrombectomy for AIS due to LVO, with or without IVT, and for 24 hours afterward, keep blood pressure <180/105 mmHg; no specific drug is preferred. The source labels this recommendation weak against intervention.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 4; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: Avoid individualised blood pressure management guided by pre-procedural pressure values during thrombectomy for AIS due to LVO, with or without IVT.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 4; recommendation 2

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Intensive reduction after successful thrombectomy
recommendations.text: Do not actively lower systolic pressure to <140 mmHg in the first 24 hours after successful thrombectomy for AIS due to LVO, with or without IVT.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 4; recommendation 3

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Avoid pressure drops during thrombectomy
recommendations.text: Avoid systolic blood pressure drops in AIS due to LVO undergoing thrombectomy, with or without IVT.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 4; recommendation 4

recommendations.section: PICO 4: Complete reperfusion and induced hypertension
recommendations.text: Do not induce hypertension after thrombectomy for AIS due to LVO when successful reperfusion is mTICI 3. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 4; consensus 1

recommendations.text: Do not routinely use vasopressors to raise pressure in deteriorating AIS patients who have not received IVT or thrombectomy.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 5; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: If deterioration without IVT or thrombectomy is suspected or shown to be haemodynamic, first stop pressure-lowering drugs, give intravenous fluids and use nonpharmacological pressure-raising measures. Only then consider cautious vasopressors with close blood pressure monitoring. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 5; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 6: Previous oral antihypertensives in AIS
recommendations.text: Do not routinely continue pre-existing oral blood pressure treatment during acute ischaemic stroke.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 6; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: In AIS with dysphagia, withhold previous oral antihypertensives until swallowing recovers or a nasogastric tube is available. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 6; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Intensive reduction in spontaneous ICH
recommendations.text: For acute spontaneous ICH with systolic pressure 150–220 mmHg, the net benefit of intensive lowering remains uncertain. Recruit to ongoing randomised trials; no recommendation strength is assigned.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 7; recommendation 1

recommendations.section: PICO 7: Small or moderate ICH pressure target
recommendations.text: For minor or moderate ICH with haematoma volume <30 mL, lower systolic pressure to <140 mmHg within 6 hours of symptom onset to limit haematoma expansion. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 7; consensus 1

recommendations.text: In spontaneous ICH, avoid lowering systolic pressure by >70 mmHg from baseline or actively below 110 mmHg. Be cautious with initial systolic pressure >220 mmHg, haematoma volume >30 mL or planned haematoma evacuation. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 7; consensus 2

recommendations.text: In acute ICH, favour treatment directed at a blood pressure target over regimens defined by a fixed antihypertensive agent. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 7; consensus 3

recommendations.section: PICO 7: ICH treatment timing and maintenance
recommendations.text: For spontaneous ICH <30 mL, begin antihypertensive treatment as early as possible, ideally within 2 hours of onset. Reduce systolic pressure to <140 mmHg while limiting variability; maintain <140 mmHg in the subacute period up to 7 days. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 7; consensus 4

recommendations.section: PICO 8: Previous oral antihypertensives in ICH
recommendations.text: In acute ICH, the benefits and risks of continuing versus temporarily stopping previous oral blood pressure therapy remain uncertain; no recommendation strength is assigned.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 8; recommendation 1

recommendations.text: If acute ICH requires pressure control and swallowing is intact, continue prior oral antihypertensives to maintain the recommended range. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 8; consensus 1

recommendations.section: PICO 8: ICH with dysphagia or impaired consciousness
recommendations.text: If acute ICH requires pressure control but dysphagia or reduced consciousness prevents oral use, temporarily withhold previous oral antihypertensives and use intravenous agents until swallowing recovers or a nasogastric tube is available. Consensus 10/10.
recommendations.sourceReference: Table 11, images aakag004fx26-1.jpg through aakag004fx26-3.jpg; individual PICO boxes; PICO 8; consensus 2

coverage.scope: All formal recommendations and good-practice/consensus statements
